Record Class GridLayout

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Record
de.schladebeck.fx.grid.GridLayout
Record Components:
columnOrder - ranges of model columns in view order, hidden ones included; empty for the natural order
columnWidths - model columns whose width the user or code set, and that width
hiddenColumns - hidden model columns
sortKeys - the columns the rows are sorted by, the first one decides; empty when unsorted
frozenColumns - number of frozen leading columns
frozenRows - number of frozen leading rows
zoom - zoom factor
columnNames - names of the model columns the other parts mention, to find them again
public record GridLayout(List<GridLayout.ColumnRange> columnOrder, Map<Integer,Double> columnWidths, Set<Integer> hiddenColumns, List<SortKey> sortKeys, int frozenColumns, int frozenRows, double zoom, Map<Integer,String> columnNames) extends Record

What a user arranged in a grid: column order, widths and visibility, sorting, frozen columns and rows, and zoom. Get it with Grid.getLayout(), store it as a string with encode(), and bring it back with decode(String) and Grid.setLayout(GridLayout):

preferences.put("grid", grid.getLayout().encode());
grid.setLayout(GridLayout.decode(preferences.get("grid", null)));   // nothing saved yet: no change

Only what differs from the defaults is kept, so a layout stays small for any number of columns: the order as ranges of model columns, and only widths the user or code set. Column indices are model columns, and the names of the columns a layout mentions are kept with it: a layout saved before columns were added or removed is applied by name, and leaves out what it cannot find.

    • decode

      public static GridLayout decode(String text)
      Reads the form written by encode(). Missing or unreadable parts get their defaults: natural column order, default widths, nothing hidden, unsorted, nothing frozen, zoom 1. Widths and zoom that are not positive finite numbers are left out.
      Parameters:
      text - the encoded layout, may be null
      Returns:
      the layout, or null for null or blank text, so restoring nothing changes nothing
